title: Folate and vitamin B-12 status in relation to anemia, macrocytosis, and cognitive impairment in older Americans in the age of folic acid fortification
authors: Morris MS, Jacques PF, Rosenberg IH, Selhub J
population: Adults aged 60 years and over in the US National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 1999-2002, after mandatory fortification, with normal serum creatinine and without stroke, alcoholism, recent anaemia therapy, or liver, thyroid or coronary disease; mean age 70 years
funder: Supported by USDA agreement no. 58-1950-9-001 and NIH no. R03 AG021536-01.
result: Low B12 status (serum B12 below 148 pmol/L or methylmalonic acid above 210 nmol/L) affected 25%; the combination of low B12 status and serum folate above 59 nmol/L about 4%. In those with low B12 status, high against normal serum folate was associated with anaemia (OR 3.1, 95% CI 1.5 to 6.6) and cognitive impairment, a Digit Symbol-Coding score below 34 (OR 2.6, 1.1 to 6.1). With normal B12 status, high serum folate was associated with less cognitive impairment (OR 0.4, 0.2 to 0.9); interaction P < 0.05. The authors note that experimental investigation of this question is unethical.
